You are a debugging assistant. You have access to the source code of the system under test (SUT), the failing test case (signature + snippet), the current issue report describing the failure, and several recent issue reports that have been pre-filtered by an external semantic retrieval model (SBERT) to be the most relevant to this failure among recent reports.

Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– likely-relevant recent bug reports,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.
Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Diagnosis:
The failure occurs when writing PAX headers for entries with long or non-ASCII names in a tar archive using TarArchiveOutputStream in LONGFILE_POSIX mode. The test tries to write a directory with a name containing non-ASCII characters (ö - \u00f6) which triggers the writing of PAX headers. The current bug report states that when the directory name is longer than 100 bytes, writing PAX headers leads to an IOException because the size recorded in the entry header doesn't match the actual bytes requested to write.

Analyzing putArchiveEntry:
- When the entry name length in bytes exceeds the standard tar limit (100 bytes), if the longFileMode is LONGFILE_POSIX, it sets a PAX header "path" with the entry name.
- If addPaxHeadersForNonAsciiNames is true and the entry name is non-ASCII, another "path" header is added.
- If there are PAX headers, writePaxHeaders is called.

Analyzing writePaxHeaders:
- This method creates a special PAX header entry with a name "./PaxHeaders.X/" + stripped version of the original entry name.
- This PAX header entry has a size set to the length of the UTF-8 encoded PAX header data.
- The headers data is computed by writing lines consisting of length, key, value, and a newline.
- The size is adjusted in a loop to account for changes in line length due to size number changes or UTF-8 encoding.
- Then the PAX header entry is put with putArchiveEntry(pex), data is written, and the entry is closed.

The issue:
The IOException message: "request to write '114' bytes exceeds size in header of '0' bytes for entry ..." suggests that the TarArchiveEntry used for the PAX headers might have a size of 0 or incorrect size at the time of writing, causing a failure in the write() call.

Possible reasons:
- The PAX header entry's size might not be correctly set before putArchiveEntry is called.
- The name of the PAX header entry might be too long and is forcibly truncated at 100 bytes as seen in the code (lines 459-461), which might be affecting subsequent handling.
- The size calculation for the PAX header entry is based on the header data's UTF-8 byte length, and that size is set correctly in line 487.
- However, putArchiveEntry calls putArchiveEntry again recursively when writing a long entry name in LONGFILE_POSIX mode, which can cause state corruption or mismatch in size.
- The line putArchiveEntry(pex) in writePaxHeaders ultimately calls putArchiveEntry on the PAX entry. Because the PAX entry's name might be long (even though truncated), if the name length triggers the longFileMode behavior in putArchiveEntry, it might cause size inconsistencies.
- The test triggers addPaxHeadersForNonAsciiNames=true, so the PAX header writing is exercised.
- The error message refers to size in header of '0' bytes, indicating the TarArchiveEntry size field was not correctly set or recognized at write time.

The test snippet confirms that setAddPaxHeadersForNonAsciiNames(true) is set, and a non-ASCII directory name is created and passed to putArchiveEntry.

Recent bug reports mention issues with long names and PAX headers. The recursion and truncation in the writePaxHeaders call and handling of size in putArchiveEntry seem to be the root of the bug.

Summary:
The bug is caused by inconsistency in size when writing PAX headers for long or non-ASCII names with LONGFILE_POSIX mode. Specifically, the PAX header entry size is either not correctly set or gets reset to zero during recursive calls or truncation of the PAX headers entry name. This leads to an IOException when the actual bytes written exceed the 0 size specified in the header.

The faulty logic likely resides in the interaction between TarArchiveOutputStream.putArchiveEntry (recursive call when writing long entry names) and TarArchiveOutputStream.writePaxHeaders (handling entry name truncation, size setting, and recursion). This causes size information not to be set or reset properly for the PAX header entry.
org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.tar.TarArchiveOutputStream.putArchiveEntry(org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.tar.TarArchiveEntry)
org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.tar.TarArchiveOutputStream.writePaxHeaders(java.lang.String, java.util.Map)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
